title: Wine Tasting Note Failure Rate
dataSources: CellarTracker bottles (`cellartracker:bottle`), Vivino wines (`vivino:wine`), spirits bottles (`spirit:bottle`), and wine tasting notes (`wine:tasting`).
app: CellarTracker bottle exports, Vivino wine scans, spirits inventory logs, and tasting note journals forwarded to Splunk HEC.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=wine:tasting
| eval status_value=lower(coalesce(tasting_status,"unknown"))
| eval failed=if(match(status_value,"error|fail|alert|overdue|late|stale|breach"),1,0)
| stats count as events, sum(failed) as failed_events by tasting_type
| eval failure_pct=round(100*failed_events/events,1)
| sort - failure_pct - failed_events
description: Measures how often wine tasting note records land in an unhealthy or exception state for each tasting type.
value: A plain failure-rate view highlights noisy devices, flaky automations, and habits that repeatedly slip.
implementation: Normalize tasting_status values into good or bad states and review the failure percentage per tasting type.
visualization: Bar chart of failure percentage by entity.
grandmaExplanation: It turns which parts of your wine tasting note data keep ending up in a bad state instead of working cleanly.
